thread:
alex: Hey team — noticed a perf dip on canary for the init/gen separation branch. Wall-clock P50 up ~12% on small-chat workloads after the scheduler change :thinking_face:

maya: Ugh. Where is it showing up? decode latency or prefill queuing?

alex: Mostly in gen (decode) tail. Prefill batches look smaller as expected, but decode stage queues up and we see kernel rebinds and extra memcpy ops in the traces. Attached quick flame: https://redwood.internal/prof/xyz (short-lived).

sam: Interesting — did the kernel selector start favoring the quantized fallback kernels when queue sizes oscillate? We saw something similar when token budgets were tightened.

alex: Yep. Profiler shows frequent kernel swaps at the stage boundary when batch sizes drop below 8. Kernel selector picks the int4 fallback path, then the next request pushes it back to fp16 path -> warmup cost.

jordan: Could be queue-policy hysteresis. If prefill separation splits batches early, decode sees many small bursts. Maybe we need a 'phase-hold' that keeps decode kernels pinned for N seconds after a warm-up batch.

maya: Agreed. Also KV cache drains look noisy: threads show repeated KV warmup RPCs because decode starts before prefill KV warmed. If we add a short KV-stabilize window (50-200ms) after prefill completes, it might reduce decode jitter.

alex: Proposed quick config (experiment):
```
batching: 
  prefill: {min_batch: 4, max_wait_ms: 20}
  decode:  {min_batch: 2, max_wait_ms: 8, phase_hold_ms: 120}
token_budget: {target_tokens: 96, bias: decode_pref}
kernel_selector: {hysteresis_ms: 150, preserve_on_swap: true}
kv: {stabilize_ms: 100}
queue_policy: round_robin_by_phase: false
```

sam: That looks reasonable as a quick A/B. I would lower decode.max_wait_ms to 4 in a high-QPS test to avoid latency blowouts. Also enable `preserve_on_swap` so we avoid the memcpy penalty.

alex: Ran a micro-canary overnight with phase_hold_ms=120 and kernel_selector.hysteresis_ms=150. Results: p50 unchanged, p95 decode dropped 9%, p99 dropped 6%, overall tokens/sec improved ~3%. CPU memcpy spikes reduced in traces.

maya: Nice! Did you run the cost regression check? Make sure bigger batches aren't causing more GPU memory churn on dedicated nodes.

alex: Checked dedicated staging — memory stable. We still saw a tiny increase in avg batch size for prefill (expected) but nothing near OOM.

jordan: Next steps: 1) Run the change across more models (long-form & instruction), 2) add a small metric to Console for kernel_swap_rate by model+phase, 3) add an infra-bot alert if kernel_swap_rate > 0.1 swaps/sec for 5m.

infra-bot: scheduling job "kernel-swap-metric" -> queued. Will collect 1h samples and post summary to #eng-runtime.

sam: One caution — for low-QPS single-tenant Dedicated customers, the phase_hold may increase per-request latency. We should gate the rollout by traffic pattern signal and only enable where QPS > 5 or where tokens/sec > X.

maya: Yep, add rollout policy: enable where estimated steady-state batch rate > 10 bps or traffic_mode == bursty.

alex: I'll open a PR with the config and add experiment flags. Thanks all, nice to see the kernel hysteresis + KV stabilize combo helped.

sam: Thanks — can you paste the flame link and the micro-canary numbers in the PR so SRE/product can review? :+1:

alex: Will do.
